title: DeepSaDe: Learning Neural Networks That Guarantee Domain Constraint Satisfaction
authors: Kshitij Goyal, Sebastijan Dumancic, Hendrik Blockeel
venue: AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, vol. 38, no. 11
conclusions: DeepSaDe enforces universally-quantified logical domain constraints (if x satisfies P then f(x) must satisfy C) over a bounded input domain, guaranteeing satisfaction for ALL inputs in that domain, not just training examples.

The guarantee is achieved training-time, at the network's last (output) layer: each batch update solves a MaxSMT (Maximum Satisfiability Modulo Theories, via the Z3 solver) problem to pick last-layer weights that satisfy the constraint set, falling back to a faster line search first; earlier layers still use ordinary gradient descent.
This gives per-instance/by-construction guarantees rather than a soft penalty: the network is only accepted/updated when the constraint holds, so violation is structurally impossible after each step.

Empirically DeepSaDe reaches 100% constraint accuracy (zero counterexamples, AdI=0) on five constrained-learning use cases, versus regularization baselines that leave exploitable counterexamples (e.g. one baseline at 93.5% constraint accuracy with counterexamples near 97% of instances).

The guarantee has a large computational cost: 10x-500x more training time than unconstrained/regularization baselines, attributed to the MaxSMT solving overhead; predictive accuracy is comparable to baselines on most use cases.

The constraints handled are per-instance logical/numerical relationships (sums, ratios, inequalities, disjunctions/conjunctions), not dataset-level or transductive aggregate-count constraints like the caps used in our paper.

The citation is used purely as one example of a training-time, by-construction hard-guarantee mechanism (contrasted with our soft/bounded transductive penalty), not claimed to solve the same transductive count-cap problem.
